reviews.title: Bid, Ask, Last, Spread, and Midpoint in a Frequently Updating Quote
reviews.learningObjective: Distinguish a quoted bid, ask and last trade; compute spread and midpoint while identifying unavailable execution evidence.
reviews.evidenceProcedure: Subtract bid from ask in dollars per share; divide the sum by two for midpoint. Keep the unrounded midpoint for calculations. Verify quote time, venue and size separately.
reviews.sourceScope: General SEC definition; original synthetic examples; no historical executions independently established.
reviews.workedCase: FICTIONAL bid $10.00, ask $10.08, last $10.03: spread=$0.08; midpoint=$10.04.
reviews.counterexample: Neither midpoint nor last trade is a guaranteed price for a new order.
reviews.freshTransfer: FICTIONAL: bid $19.95, ask $20.10 and last $20.00. Calculate the spread and unrounded midpoint with units. Explain whether any of these values proves a 1,000-share execution; name the missing evidence.
reviews.rights: Link and original summary only; no article or market-data reproduction.

reviews.title: Compare Quote Width Without Jumping Ahead to Liquidity Analysis
reviews.learningObjective: Compare absolute quote widths without inferring executable size or guaranteed liquidity.
reviews.evidenceProcedure: Compute ask minus bid for each quote in dollars per share. A comparison of widths leaves size, timestamp, venue and price impact unresolved.
reviews.sourceScope: General SEC definition; original synthetic examples; no historical executions independently established.
reviews.workedCase: FICTIONAL spreads: $20.00/$20.05 has $0.05 width; $20.00/$20.30 has $0.30 width.
reviews.counterexample: A narrow spread for ten displayed shares cannot guarantee a 1,000-share fill.
reviews.freshTransfer: FICTIONAL: compare $8.40/$8.48 with $8.40/$8.56. Calculate each spread; then explain why neither spread establishes a 1,000-share fill and identify what evidence is missing.
reviews.rights: Link and original summary only; no article or market-data reproduction.

reviews.title: Order Selection, Fills, Partial Fills, and Execution Control — Market Orders
reviews.learningObjective: Explain why a market-order execution price can differ from a last trade or displayed ask.
reviews.evidenceProcedure: Separate the last transaction from the current quote, and the displayed quantity from the intended order quantity. Use actual execution reports to establish fills; do not manufacture missing prices.
reviews.sourceScope: General SEC definition; original synthetic examples; no historical executions independently established.
reviews.workedCase: FICTIONAL: buy 100 shares when displayed ask is $5.08 with only 20 shares; full fill at $5.08 is unproven.
reviews.counterexample: A past $5.00 last trade cannot promise the next 100-share buy at $5.00.
reviews.freshTransfer: FICTIONAL: the last trade is $6.00; the ask is $6.08 for 25 shares; a proposed market buy is 200 shares. Identify which prices and quantities are observations and which total execution cost remains unknowable. State when NO TRADE is reasonable.
reviews.rights: Link and original summary only; no article or market-data reproduction.

reviews.title: Order Selection, Fills, Partial Fills, and Execution Control — Marketable Limit Orders
reviews.learningObjective: Apply a buy-limit price constraint while distinguishing partial execution from a guaranteed full fill.
reviews.evidenceProcedure: For a buy limit, compare each possible execution price with the limit; total filled quantity still requires execution evidence. A quote touch alone is insufficient.
reviews.sourceScope: General SEC definition; original synthetic examples; no historical executions independently established.
reviews.workedCase: FICTIONAL 100-share buy limit $5.06 sees 30 offered shares at $5.06; the rest might not fill.
reviews.counterexample: Merely touching a buy limit in past prices does not establish that the whole order executed.
reviews.freshTransfer: FICTIONAL: a 100-share buy limit is $6.10, the current ask is $6.08 for 10 shares. State the permitted execution-price boundary and whether the remaining 90 shares are guaranteed. Distinguish marketability now from a later quote change.
reviews.rights: Link and original summary only; no article or market-data reproduction.
